note: Commercially he fits and then some: an international project manager on expatriate assignment who called $9,000 'a fair investment', chose the higher tier himself and raised no money objection at any point. He misses on all three health and starting-point criteria, decisively. Health is not the neglected corner of an otherwise sorted life, it is an active crisis — gallbladder removed three weeks ago, hypertension that peaked at 200 and is newly medicated, a new fatty liver diagnosis, and 125 kg. The ask is rescue, not good-to-great: 'I need to change. I need to get into shape and I need to lose weight.' And he is the deconditioned prospect the exclusion was written to keep out — never trained consistently, disliked the gym, and self-describes as 'not very fit now'. This is the second data point for the existing finding that the buying population is wider than the stated ICP, and it sharpens it: the highest-value close in this batch sits outside the ICP on every health criterion, and the stated ICP still contains no clinical criterion that would have caught it.
